Order
This Criminal Miscellaneous Case has been filed under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (`BNSS' for short) by the sole accused in S.C.No.962/2020 on the files of the Special Court for trial of offences relating to atrocities against Women and Children including Protection of Children against Sexual Offences (`POCSO') Cases, Kozhikode, seeking the following prayers:
"i) quash Annexure-A2 final report in Crime No.570/2020 of Payyoli Police Station, Kozhikode Distruct numbered as S.C.No.962/2020 on the files of the Hon'ble District and Sessions Court,
Kozhikode and all further proceedings against the petitioner pursuant to the same;
ii) issue any other appropriate order or direction as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit in the interest of justice."
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner on admission.
Also 2024:KER:83144 heard the learned Public Prosecutor in detail.
Perused the records.

3. Here the prosecution alleges commission of offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 496,
406 of the Indian Penal Code (`IPC' for short) and Sections 3(2)(v) and 3(1)(w)(i) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (`SC/ST POA Act' for short).

entities.text: Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The prosecution allegation is that the accused, who doesn't belong either to Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe community, offered to marry the victim, who is a member of Hindu Pulaya community of Scheduled Caste, starting from May, 2017, and on the said promise she was subjected to repeated sexual intercourse in between May, 2017 and 17.04.2019, after effecing a fake marriage by tying thali on her.
Thereafter on 14.08.2020 the accused married another lady.
Further the accused also obtained Rs.3 lakh from the defacto complainant during the said relation and thereby committed breach of trust also.

4. While canvassing quashment of the proceedings, the learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the allegations are false and the relationship is purely consensual and therefore none of the offences would attract.

Whereas it is submitted by the learned Public Prosecutor that going by the prosecution records,
the allegations are well made out, prima facie, and in such a case, quashment prayer is liable to fail,

2 even though the defacto complainant filed an affidavit supporting settlement of this crime.

sentences.text:
It is submitted by the learned Public Prosecutor that settling serious offences like murder, dacoity, etc.
could not be considered merely acting on the affidavit subsequently filed by the victim since the prosecution has the right to corroborate the version of the victim with her 164 statement recorded during investigation.
6. I have gone through the prosecution case to address the rival arguments.

In this matter FIS would recite that the victim, a member of Hindu Pulaya Scheduled Caste community, was married earlier with one Babu as on 09.02.2004 and thereafter the defacto complainant was living separately from him since there was no child.

According to the defacto complainant, during June, 2016, started residence at her own house after leaving the company of her husband and in the meantime the accused constantly contacted her through telephone and informed his desire to marry the defacto complainant, though he is a member of Nair community, 2024:KER:83144 knowing her caste identity
. During this relationship, he obtained Rs.3 lakh from the defacto complainant on 2 occasions.
Further she was taken to his residence starting from May, 2017 till 17.04.2019 and subjected her to repeated sexual intercourse, repeating promise of marriage.
Thereafter he tied a thali on her and continued sexual relationship.
While so, he married another lady, thereby committed the above offences.

In the facts of the case, it is discernible that at the time when the relationship continued and as of now the earlier legal marriage between the defacto complainant and her former husband has been continuing and therefore the promise of marriage is an absolute impossibility through the entire period of relationship.

Therefore, relationship otherwise is to be held as consensual in a case where the defacto complainant now filed an affidavit stating that she has no grievance, as the money transaction and other disputes have been settled.
7. Having considered the factual matrix of the case in the above line, I am of the view that the quashment prayer is liable to succeed.
In the result, this Criminal Miscellaneous Case stands allowed.
Annexure-A2 final report in Crime No.570/2020 of Payyoli Police Station, 2024:KER:83144 Kozhikode District, against the petitioner stands quashed.
